terms.name: Achievement badge
terms.definition: A collectible marker awarded for a milestone and displayed on a profile, often shown greyed out before it is earned so the set is visible.

terms.name: Anchor positioning
terms.definition: A CSS mechanism that tethers one element to another, sizing and placing it against its anchor and trying fallback positions when the default one would overflow.

terms.name: Asymmetric easing
terms.definition: Giving a state change and its reverse different curves or durations, usually a quick confident exit and a slower entrance, so the two directions do not feel identical.

terms.name: Bauhaus style
terms.definition: A style reduced to primary red, yellow, and blue on off-white, elementary circles, triangles, and squares, and undecorated sans serif type.

terms.name: Brushing
terms.definition: Dragging a selection across one chart to highlight the same records in every linked view.

terms.name: Caret
terms.definition: The blinking marker showing where typed text will be inserted, moved by clicking, by arrow keys, or by dragging on touch.

terms.name: Chevron
terms.definition: The small angle bracket used as a directional marker: down means this opens, right means this goes deeper, in breadcrumbs it means next level.

terms.name: Color font
terms.definition: A font whose glyphs carry their own colors, gradients, or layers, with a palette the page can override rather than a single ink.

terms.name: Column offset
terms.definition: Pushing a column away from the grid's start so it begins on a later line, leaving deliberate empty tracks rather than an element to fill them.

terms.name: Consistent help
terms.definition: Keeping the same help route, a contact link, a chat launcher, a self-help pane, in the same relative place on every page so a stuck reader can find it again.

terms.name: Count-up animation
terms.definition: Animating a number toward its value instead of setting it, often with digits rolling like an odometer so the change is legible.

terms.name: Data-ink ratio
terms.definition: Tufte's measure of chart economy: the share of ink that would be missed if erased, with everything else a candidate for deletion.

terms.name: Diff viewer
terms.definition: The view that puts two versions of a text against each other, side by side or interleaved, marking every line added, removed or changed and aligning what did not.

terms.name: Double click
terms.definition: Two clicks inside a short interval on the same spot, treated as one gesture that opens, edits, or selects a word rather than activating twice.

terms.name: Duotone
terms.definition: An image rendered in two colours instead of full colour, mapping its shadows to one hue and its highlights to another so photography joins the brand palette.

terms.name: Emphasis level
terms.definition: A three-rung text hierarchy, high, medium and disabled, ranked by stepping the opacity of one foreground colour instead of naming a separate colour for each rung.

terms.name: Faceted filter
terms.definition: A panel of grouped checkboxes and ranges that narrows a result set, each option usually showing how many results it would leave.

terms.name: File upload
terms.definition: A control that takes files, by opening the system picker from a button or by accepting a drop into a marked area.

terms.name: Flowchart
terms.definition: A diagram of steps in boxes joined by arrows, read rather than operated, and now more often generated from a few lines of text than drawn by hand.

terms.name: FOIT
terms.definition: The blank period when a browser hides text entirely rather than show it in a fallback face while the web font loads.

terms.name: Full bleed
terms.definition: An element that breaks past the content column to span the whole viewport width while its neighbours stay constrained.

terms.name: Gradient border
terms.definition: An outline filled with a gradient rather than a single color, usually built from a conic or linear gradient behind a masked shape so the hue travels around the edge.

terms.name: Header association
terms.definition: The markup that ties a data cell to its row and column headers, so a cell read on its own still says what it is.

terms.name: Hover card
terms.definition: A rich preview panel that appears on hover over a link or an avatar, summarising what is behind it.

terms.name: Image well
terms.definition: An editable image view that shows its current picture and accepts a replacement dragged or pasted straight into it.

terms.name: Interface metaphor
terms.definition: Explaining a system by dressing it as something the user already knows: the desktop, the trash can, the folder, the shopping cart.

terms.name: Ken Burns effect
terms.definition: A slow pan and zoom across a still image that gives it motion, named after the documentary filmmaker who made the technique famous.

terms.name: Lawn mower pattern
terms.definition: A scanning shape for tables where the eye runs across one row, drops down and runs back the other way, mowing the cells in alternating directions.

terms.name: Line clamp
terms.definition: Cutting a block of text off after a fixed number of lines, with an ellipsis at the end of the last one.

terms.name: Long press
terms.definition: A press held in place for a moment before release, used to reveal secondary actions, enter a rearrange mode, or open a contextual menu.

terms.name: Meatball menu
terms.definition: An overflow menu whose trigger is three horizontal dots, usually sitting at the end of a row or a card.

terms.name: Miller columns
terms.definition: A browsing layout of side-by-side columns where selecting an item in one column fills the next with its children, keeping the whole path visible.

terms.name: Mostly fluid
terms.definition: A responsive pattern where a multi column grid stretches with the viewport up to a maximum width, then centres, stacking only on the smallest screens.

terms.name: Navigation menu
terms.definition: A menu of destinations rather than commands, where opening an item moves you somewhere instead of running an action.

terms.name: Obstruction
terms.definition: Putting deliberate hurdles in front of an action the business does not want taken, so the effort itself does the discouraging.

terms.name: Order summary
terms.definition: The persistent panel beside a checkout listing items, quantities, and every cost line, kept visible so nothing about the total arrives as a surprise.

terms.name: Page title
terms.definition: The document title, the first thing a screen reader speaks and the only label a reader has when picking between tabs, windows, and history entries.

terms.name: Picture in picture
terms.definition: A small always on top window that keeps video or navigation visible in a corner while the reader works in another app or scrolls another page.

terms.name: Popover arrow
terms.definition: The small triangle joining a popover or tooltip to the thing it belongs to, which flips and slides as the popover repositions.

terms.name: Progressive blur
terms.definition: A blur whose strength ramps across a region instead of applying evenly, so content fades into softness toward an edge rather than stopping at a hard line.

terms.name: Quick settings tile
terms.definition: A one tap button or toggle an app contributes to the system control surface, so one feature can be reached without opening the app.

terms.name: Reading progress
terms.definition: A bar tied to scroll position that shows how much of an article remains, usually pinned to the top edge and filling as the reader descends.

terms.name: Review cursor
terms.definition: A second cursor a screen reader user can move over the screen to read text without moving the system focus, so inspecting a region does not disturb the app.

terms.name: Sans-serif
terms.definition: A typeface drawn without finishing strokes on the ends of its stems, which is the default register of most interface type.

terms.name: Scroll snap
terms.definition: Snap positions declared on a scroll container so scrolling settles on a chosen item edge instead of stopping wherever momentum runs out.

terms.name: Selection handle
terms.definition: The draggable grip at each end of a touch text selection, used to widen or narrow the range a finger cannot adjust precisely.

terms.name: Sign language interpretation
terms.definition: A signed track alongside video, presented as an inset or a companion stream, for readers whose first language is a sign language rather than the written caption text.

terms.name: Smart quotes
terms.definition: The curved opening and closing quotation marks a typeface actually draws, as opposed to the straight vertical marks inherited from typewriters.

terms.name: Speculative loading
terms.definition: Fetching, or fully rendering, a page before the reader asks for it, on a guess about where they go next, so the navigation is already done when the click lands.

terms.name: Stat
terms.definition: A single number shown large with a label and often a change indicator, the unit a dashboard is built from.

terms.name: Strikethrough
terms.definition: A rule drawn through the middle of text to mark it as removed, superseded, or no longer the current price.

terms.name: Swiss style
terms.definition: The Swiss modernist system of a strict grid, flush left sans serif type, asymmetric layout, and objective photography, still the base of clean UI layout.

terms.name: Target spacing
terms.definition: The exception that lets an undersized control pass when no other target falls inside a 24 pixel circle centred on it, trading size for clearance.

terms.name: Timeout warning
terms.definition: A warning before a session or form expires with a simple way to extend it, so a slower reader does not lose their work silently.

terms.name: Track
terms.definition: The groove a slider thumb or scrollbar travels along, usually drawn as filled before the handle and empty after it.

terms.name: Typeface
terms.definition: The designed set of letterforms itself, as distinct from a font, which is one particular file or instance you actually use.

terms.name: Vernacular web
terms.definition: The amateur homepage look of the GeoCities era: tiled backgrounds, sparkle GIFs, under construction signs, midi music, and hit counters.

terms.name: Wheel picker
terms.definition: A spinning drum of values that snaps to the item under a fixed selection line, the iOS way of choosing from a short list.

terms.name: Zero state
terms.definition: The first-run screen a feature shows before any data exists, written to teach the feature rather than to report emptiness.
